items.title: Egyptian mummies coming to Sarawak next year
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak is set to host a major international exhibition featuring artefacts and actual human remains dating back over 5,000 years from the National Archaeological Museum of Florence, Italy, next year. Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the exclusive six-month exhibition, titled 'Egyptian Mummies: Journey Towards Immortality', will be held at the Borneo Cultures Museum (BCM) starting July next year. He said the Sarawak Museum Department's success in bringing in such a global-scale exhibition demonstrates the agency's capability and proactive approach in establishing strategic collaborations with world-renowned museums.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 20, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Interpol issues Red Notice Interpol has issued a Red Notice against Serba Dinamik founder Datuk Mohd Abdul Karim Abdullah, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Samsuri questions timing Perikatan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has questioned the timing of the coalition's deregistration. Shuhaily faces charges Border agency chief Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will face two charges of voluntarily causing hurt tomorrow.

items.title: ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over US$35bil worth of Nvidia chip orders
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than three million of Nvidia's new RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards with a collective sticker price of over US$35 billion, two people familiar with the matter said, in a rush for a less powerful but export-compliant chip amid US restrictions on trade with China. US-based chipmaker Nvidia has told customers and partners it cannot guarantee that it can fill the orders because demand from Chinese technology companies far exceeds planned production, the two sources and a third person familiar with the matter said. The RTX PRO 5500 is a workstation chip, designed for powerful professional computers rather than the large data-centre clusters that use Nvidia's most advanced AI processors.

items.title: 16-year-old girl rescued from suspected sex exploitation in Arau
items.summary: KANGAR: Police rescued a 16-year-old girl suspected of being sexually exploited by a prostitution syndicate through a social media application during a raid at a premises in Arau yesterday. Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said two men were also arrested during the raid under Op Noda at 11.15pm. "During the raid, police arrested the two men, who are suspected of promoting prostitution through the MiChat application and sexually exploiting the victim.

items.title: Ministry, UM have no plans to act against student rep over 'tough' question - Zambry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Higher Education Ministry and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a "tough" question during the i-Future programme. Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the ministry maintained its position that students' right to freedom of expression must be respected, while condemning any form of abuse, insults or threats directed at the student on social media. Respect students' right to speak up.

items.title: PM: TuJu offers local alternative for road navigation
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the alternative was proposed due to security concerns over information and data on citizens' movements, given that the Waze application is subject to Israeli laws. He said the matter was among the topics discussed at the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee, which he chaired today to review evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation's preparedness and digital sovereignty. "Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).

items.title: Haze: Schools remain open in six states, KL and Putrajaya tomorrow, outdoor activities halted
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze. In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) would operate as usual. In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.

items.title: i-City unveils AI-powered homes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: i-City has launched AI Living @ i-City, a residential concept combining home automation, robotics, wellness technology and artificial intelligence (AI), with its first development comprising 500 units. Datuk Firdaus, chairman of Firdaus & Associates (the development's lead marketing agency), said the campaign aims to explain how AI and robotics could be incorporated into residential living, including home security, elderly care and lifestyle management. AI Living builds on i-City's technology-focused development, which includes AIWEC, established in collaboration with Chinese robotics company AgiBot.

items.title: From Waze to TuJu? Anwar backs Malaysian navigation app over data security concerns
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this alternative has been proposed due to security risks concerning information and data on citizens’ movements, given that the Waze application is subject to the laws of the Israeli government. He noted that this matter was among the topics discussed while chairing the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) today, which aimed to examine evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation’s preparedness and digital sovereignty. “Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).

items.title: No action against UM student over viral ‘tough’ question, says Zambry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a “tough” question during the i-Future programme. Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the ministry maintained its position that students’ right to freedom of expression must be respected, while condemning any form of abuse, insults or threats directed at the student on social media. Respect students’ right to speak up.

items.title: LYC Healthcare appeals against delisting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: LYC Healthcare Bhd has appealed against the commencement of delisting proceedings, putting its scheduled removal from Bursa Malaysia on hold pending the exchange's decision. In a bourse filing today, the healthcare services provider said it submitted the appeal on Oct 20, ahead of the Oct 26 deadline. The company said the delisting would be deferred pending Bursa Malaysia's decision on the appeal.

items.title: RTD warns of fake TikTok account offering driving licences without tests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has confirmed that a TikTok account using the name Ahmad Mushidi, which offers driving licences without requiring applicants to sit for tests, is fake. The RTD said it had received complaints about advertisements on the social media platform offering driving licences without the need to attend classes or undergo driving tests. A check of the TikTok account found that it was offering Class B2 motorcycle licences for RM350 and full Class B (B Full) motorcycle licences for RM380, without requiring applicants to sit for RTD tests.

items.title: No driving licences without tests: JPJ warns against fake TikTok promotions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has denied the authenticity of a TikTok advertisement offering driving licences without the need to take a test. In a statement today, JPJ said it received complaints regarding the advertisement, which used an account under the name ‘Ahmad Mushidi’. “JPJ wishes to emphasise that the advertisement and the account belonging to the individual named Ahmad Mushidi are fake,” the statement read.

items.title: 13 killed, 34 injured as truck crashes into tour bus in Egypt
items.summary: GIZA: A large truck crashed into a tour bus west of the Egyptian capital on Tuesday, killing 13 people and injuring 34, state media reported. Last year, nearly 6,000 people were killed in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt's state statistics agency. Last month, a bus crash in Sinai killed 22 people, including 10 Jordanian tourists.

items.title: Driver detained after dangerous overtaking in Johor Baru [WATCH]
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 38-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of endangering other road users by driving dangerously on Jalan Bakawali, Taman Johor Jaya. Seri Alam deputy police chief Superintendent Victor Genason said the man was detained at 9.35am at the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Seri Alam district police headquarters. Victor said police also seized a Proton e.MAS believed to have been used by the man during the incident.

items.title: Kampar woman loses over RM129,000 in online job scam
items.summary: Kampar District Police Chief Supt Mohamad Nazri Daud said that his department received a report yesterday from the 34-year-old victim. “Initial police investigations found that the victim saw an offer for a part-time job related to hotel bookings through social media. “The victim received a message from an unknown individual offering the job.

items.title: Schools in six states, KL and Putrajaya to operate as usual tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze. In NEGRI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MOE) would operate as usual. In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.

items.title: Four states record highest rates of drug abuse - Nada
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh. He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 people per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646). In this regard, Ruslin said Nada was focusing on enforcement, prevention programmes and community empowerment in high-risk states, targeting three main segments, namely, educational institutions, families and communities.

items.title: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis record highest drug abuse rates
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh. He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 individuals per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646). Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.

items.title: Man charged over attack on Australian MP Haines
items.summary: MELBOURNE: Australian police charged a man on Tuesday over what they alleged was a "targeted" attack with a vehicle on independent lawmaker Helen Haines. The driver had made a U-turn to get back to her after passing, Albanese said on Tuesday. "Police will allege the incident was targeted," Victoria police said.

items.title: Selangor steps up monitoring of Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government is stepping up efforts to monitor the spread of Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings in the state through the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), in cooperation with mosques and surau. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the efforts also included educating the public on the differences between Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings and the beliefs of Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah, an initiative that had been ongoing for years. "We also organise large-scale programmes to explain the differences between Ahmadiyah or Qadiani teachings and the practices of Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah," he told reporters after the launch of a collaboration involving Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), Universiti Selangor (Unisel) and the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre (STDC) here today.

items.title: Selangor Education Department cooperating with probe into schoolgirl’s death
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 20 — The Selangor State Education Department (JPN Selangor) will fully cooperate with the authorities’ investigations into the death of a Year One pupil after she experienced breathing difficulties at a school in Sepang. In a statement today, JPN Selangor said the girl was reported to have had breathing difficulties at school and was taken to hospital for treatment. “JPN Selangor extends its condolences and deepest sympathies to the pupil’s family.

items.title: 'I thought he was surrendering': Cop recounts parang attack [WATCH]
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: After 10 years in the police force, a corporal never imagined that a routine anti-drug operation would turn life-threatening when a suspect armed with a parang slashed his left arm. He said he was part of a police team that raided a house in Kampung Lalang Pepuyu, Tanah Merah, on Oct 17 as part of a special operation to curb drug abuse. "Instead, he swung the parang at me and slashed my left arm," said the 37-year-old when met today.

items.title: Police record statements over podcast video on alleged drug trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Police have opened an investigation into the circulation of a podcast video alleging that drug trafficking activities were taking place at a house of worship near the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the investigation was being conducted under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. He said the investigation was initiated following a police report lodged by the chairman of the Marathadi Madurai Veeran Temple in Kuala Lumpur last Sunday to strongly deny the allegations made in the video.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution urges Asean to translate anti-crime pledges into results
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks. Saifuddin Nasution highlighted that as Malaysia prepares to chair Asean in 2025, the country has laid a crucial foundation for regional security cooperation through the adoption of the Asean Plan of Action to Combat Transnational Crime (2026-2035) and the Melaka Declaration.

items.title: Fahmi calls for stronger Asean cooperation on child online safety
items.summary: BALI, Oct 20 — Asean countries must work together to protect children from growing online threats despite differences in their laws and approaches to internet safety, said Malaysia’s Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said countries in the region shared the challenge of keeping the internet safe for children and needed to strengthen cooperation to address these threats. Fahmi said Malaysia wanted to ensure that children below the age of 16 were unable to open social media accounts, although approaches to online safety for children could differ between Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and other Asean countries.

items.title: Prisoner charged with murdering fellow inmate at Marang prison
items.summary: Che Mohd Nazzaruddin Che Ros, 35, is accused of killing Nor Mohd Helmi Sahari in Zone 2, R10, Marang Prison, between 8.45 am and 9.15 am on Aug 24. Deputy public prosecutor Noradila Ab Latif appeared for the prosecution, while Che Mohd Nazzaruddin was unrepresented. The court fixed Nov 5 for mention of Mohd Fadli's and Nor Dhitauddin's case, and Dec 10 for Che Mohd Nazzaruddin's case.

items.title: Halal concerns prompt Jakim probe into chicken slaughtering
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) is investigating chicken slaughtering methods at a premises near Pudu Market following a video circulating on social media. Its director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee said in a statement that the probe also involved local authorities. Putrajaya member of parliament Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin had urged Jakim to investigate the slaughtering methods, halal status and where the chicken processed at the premises was supplied and sold.

items.title: DNB, MRT Corp team up for 5G coverage at RTS immigration, customs complex
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) and MRT Corp have partnered to provide indoor 5G connectivity at the Rapid Transit System's (RTS) Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security complex (ICQC) in Johor Bahru. The collaboration aims to provide comprehensive indoor 5G coverage across the RTS' ICQC complex, allowing commuters to access reliable connectivity and digital services, including ticketing, navigation, communications and mobile transactions. Azman said the RTS Link complex offered an opportunity to demonstrate the benefits of seamless indoor 5G connectivity and improve the commuter experience.

items.title: 20th AMMTC: Asean needs concrete actions to eradicate transnational crimes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks. He said the threat of transnational crime has become increasingly complex due to the misuse of digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), necessitating a faster and more integrated response from Asean member states.

items.title: SC extends deadline for Yinson privatisation intention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) has approved an extension until Nov 30, 2026, for Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd (YLSB), MISC Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) to announce their intention regarding the proposed privatisation of Yinson Holdings Bhd. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, Yinson Holdings said the SC announced this in its letter dated Oct 19, 2026. The extension will allow the parties to continue evaluating and discussing the proposed scheme.

items.title: Thai court overturns attempted rape conviction of Olympic boxing champion
items.summary: BANGKOK: A Thai appeals court overturned on Tuesday a conviction for the attempted rape of a teenage girl handed to the country's first Olympic gold medallist, but upheld his sentence for abduction. A regional appeals court in Khon Kaen dismissed the attempted rape conviction on Tuesday, saying the victim's testimony contained "inconsistencies" and there was no evidence of coercion or threats. Somluck's sentence was adjusted to two years, the court said in a media statement.

items.title: Anwar backs efforts to strengthen IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed efforts to strengthen the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, positioning it as a hub for the sharing of knowledge and expertise. He noted that Malaysia is recognised for its experience in empowering micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), strengthening economic resilience, and generating employment opportunities, expertise and experience that could potentially benefit other IsDB member countries. The IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, launched in 2019, serves as a strategic platform for the transfer of technology, expertise, and best practices in Islamic finance from Malaysia to the 56 other IsDB member countries.

items.title: Gamuda, Perak state govt ink deal to implement Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd today announced that an agreement to implement the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme (NPWSS) has been signed between the State Government of Perak, Khazanah Air Perak Sdn Bhd (KAP), and Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIPP). KAP is a 50:50 joint venture company between Gamuda and Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Perak (PKNPk), while PAIPP is KAP's wholly owned subsidiary. "The NPWSS agreement formalises PAIPP's appointment as the WTP operator to undertake the water treatment plant (WTP) Scope, including the right to abstract raw water for the Phase 1 WTP, and KAP's role in the source works scope," it said.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 20, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia recovered on Tuesday, gaining 3.83 points or 0.24 per cent to close at 1,595, supported by bargain hunting. The rebound was further supported by renewed foreign buying, with overseas investors turning net buyers for the first time this month, potentially signalling an improvement in near-term market sentiment. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin traded lower at RM331,999, while Ethereum hovered at RM9,707.

items.title: Selangor Sultan cautions royal family members against exploiting royal status
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 20 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain. “We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.

items.title: RedPlanet's adjusted FY26 profit jumps 35pct ahead of listing
items.summary: The enterprise information and communications technology (ICT) solutions provider recorded revenue of RM40.72 million, up 22.3 per cent from RM33.3 million a year earlier. On a reported basis, RedPlanet's profit increased 21.3 per cent to RM6.33 million from RM5.22 million previously. For the fourth quarter, RedPlanet posted revenue of RM7.55 million and net profit of RM1.36 million.

items.title: Muhyiddin saddened by Perikatan deregistration, warns against abuse of power in coalitions
items.summary: In a statement, Muhyiddin, who founded PN, said he was saddened by the coalition's deregistration. "However, this decision is a reminder to any party leading a coalition to act fairly towards all member parties and to always comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966," he said. Muhyiddin also cautioned against the misuse of power and position within a political coalition for the benefit of a particular party or group.

items.title: Iran prolongs talks in stalemate to influence US midterms, officials say
items.summary: DUBAI: Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's US midterm elections, senior officials say, while fears of renewed military action and deep distrust of Washington have reinforced Teheran's reluctance to strike a quick deal to end the war. "Iran is preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal with America to end the war," one of the officials said. Teheran analyst Saeed Leylaz said that, by prolonging the talks, "Iran is influencing the US election without taking any unlawful action."

items.title: Schools still first channel to seek justice for bullying, Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB) only next option, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Students struggling with bullying should seek justice through their schools first before bringing their grievances to the Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB), said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Azalina said the TAB would also evaluate the complaints received before accepting the relevant cases for mediation to prevent it from being overwhelmed with the high volume of complaints. Azalina said the rising numbers of cases reflect growing awareness on bullying, which she said would eventually reduce bullying incidents as perpetrators would realise that the TAB will hold them accountable.

items.title: Selangor Sultan warns royal family against abusing status
items.summary: KLANG: Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain. "We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.

items.title: Uphold Malay language without neglecting English, says Fadhlina
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 20 — The Malay language must be consistently upheld without neglecting English proficiency among the younger generation, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said efforts to strengthen the language should be pursued through various platforms, including public speaking competitions, which provide higher education students with opportunities to express their views through well-reasoned, knowledge-based arguments. Fadhlina said oratory competitions not only encouraged the continued use of the national language but also helped enrich vocabulary and improve language skills among the public.

items.title: One in three Americans back second execution attempt after failed one, poll finds
items.summary: WASHINGTON: One-third of Americans think the government should try a second time to put a convicted criminal to death if a first execution attempt fails, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee. The four-day poll, completed on Monday, showed 39 per cent of respondents thought the government should instead allow convicts to serve life in prison following a failed execution, while 26 per cent were not sure which was a better approach. The nationwide survey found minority public support for trying again to execute inmates who survive execution attempts, a question Tennessee now faces after Christa Pike, 50, survived two lethal injection attempts last month in Nashville.

items.title: 3 ministries will decide on school closures as haze persists, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any decision to close schools amid the ongoing haze will be made jointly by the Education Ministry (MOE), Health Ministry (MOH) and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on their respective expertise, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said the decision would be based on air quality monitoring and health considerations to ensure students' safety, while also considering the impact on learning loss if schools were closed for too long. Also present was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Bank Negara unveils tokenised bonds platform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has launched a new platform to facilitate the issuance, depository and safekeeping of tokenised bonds and sukuk. Bank Negara said the platform was developed in-house using cloud and distributed ledger technologies. It builds on the existing scripless securities depository system, which serves as the central securities depository for the wholesale financial market.

items.title: Families, seniors welcome ECRL fare discounts
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 20 — A 50 per cent discount on East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) fares for eligible passengers positions the rail service as a new, more affordable transport option particularly for families traveling with children and senior citizens. Civil servant Fairus Mohd, 42, noted that the discount allows her to bring along her three children-aged between three and seven as well as her 75-year-old mother, Jeriah Abdul Rahman, for a trip to Kuala Lumpur via the ECRL. For 60-year-old senior citizen Noril Azian Jaafar, the 50 per cent fare discount offered by the ECRL service is a highly beneficial initiative that helps save on travel costs, while also providing her with the opportunity to return to Pasir Mas, Kelantan, more frequently to visit relatives.

items.title: Haze-related school closures subject to joint ministry review, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Any decision to close schools amid the ongoing haze will be made jointly by the Education Ministry (MOE), Health Ministry (MOH) and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on their respective expertise, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said the decision would be based on air quality monitoring and health considerations to ensure students’ safety, while also considering the impact on learning loss if schools were closed for too long. Also present was Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Batu Muda tops API readings as haze worsens in 25 areas across Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Twenty-five areas nationwide remained at unhealthy air quality levels as of 4pm today, with Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 173. Three areas in Melaka also recorded unhealthy air quality: Bukit Rambai (166), Alor Gajah (156) and Bandaraya Melaka (156). A total of 35 areas recorded moderate API readings nationwide, while only eight areas had good readings.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan records fewer online crime cases and lower losses
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 20 — Online crime cases in Negeri Sembilan dropped by 268, or 10 per cent, to 2,539 as of September this year, compared with 2,807 cases in the corresponding period last year, while financial losses dropped by RM33.58 million to RM39.86 million. However, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said e-commerce fraud cases rose by 24 per cent to 828, compared with 667 in the corresponding period last year, while cases involving non-existent loans increased by 11 per cent to 404 from 365. “Investment scam cases fell by 20 per cent to 298 from 374, while total losses declined by RM24.50 million, or 66 per cent.

items.title: Court of Appeal rejects fashion designer Jovian Mandagie’s bid to overturn RM10m payment order
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Court of Appeal today dismissed fashion designer Datuk Jovian Mandagie’s appeals to set aside the High Court’s decisions granting two companies’ applications for summary judgment against him in a lawsuit over the alleged breach of friendly loan agreements. A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril and Datin Paduka Evrol Mariette Peters, dismissed the appeal by a 2-1 majority decision. Lawyer Siti Nur Athirazatti Rohizad, representing Bina Pragmatik Sdn Bhd and Cekap Air Sdn Bhd, confirmed the court’s decision when contacted by Bernama.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected in 12 states, KL this evening, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 12 states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 6pm today. The warning also covers several areas in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Larut Matang and Selama, and in Kelantan, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu and Bachok. In Terengganu, the areas affected are Hulu Terengganu, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman and Kuala Nerus, while in Pahang, the warning covers Jerantut, Rompin and Bentong.

items.title: Nilai border control officer’s death: Police record statements from 18 individuals, husband remains in remand until Oct 22
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 20 — Police have recorded statements from 18 individuals to assist in investigations into the death of an officer of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai last Thursday. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation paper would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor in the near future. Alzafny said the post-mortem found that the woman died from pressure applied to her neck.

items.title: Budget 2027 debate: Muhyiddin calls for urban poverty master plan, MP allocation law proposed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Issues concerning urban poverty, the allocation of funds for Members of Parliament (MPs), and efforts to strengthen the nation’s healthcare sector were among the topics raised during the policy-level debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today. The former prime minister said the plan should focus on housing, healthcare, employment, education, skills training, and social assistance to ensure that low-income groups also benefit from the nation’s economic development. He said the drafting of the act could be carried out by the Parliamentary Service Council, following the enforcement of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025.

items.title: Sarawak steps up preparations to co-host 2027 SEA Games
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 20 — Sarawak is intensifying preparations to co-host the 2027 SEA Games from September 18 to 29 next year, with promotional activities set to continue across the state, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly was told today. Sarawak Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the promotional activities include a torch run covering all 12 divisions in the state. Abdul Karim said Sarawak will host 18 of the 43 sports at the 2027 SEA Games, with dance sport newly included in the Sarawak cluster.

items.title: Sabah CM: RM150m Nabawan police headquarters, housing project to begin in January 2027
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 20 — The construction of the Nabawan district police headquarters (IPD) and police housing project, with an allocation ceiling of RM150 million, is expected to begin in January 2027, said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the infrastructure project aimed to strengthen security capabilities, law enforcement and service delivery to the public, particularly in Nabawan and surrounding areas. Also present were Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, Sabah State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman and Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.

items.title: Malaysia looks to put durians on the fast track to China by road, rail in three to four days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is stepping up negotiations with several countries in the region to facilitate the export of fresh durians to China by road and rail, with shipments expected to take just three to four days, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. He said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) was working closely with the Foreign Ministry and Transport Ministry to coordinate cross-border routes through Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia. “Overland shipments are expected to take only three to four days, allowing goods, particularly durians, to reach the Chinese market quickly.

items.title: States urged to gazette over 15,000ha of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia, FT
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — More than 15,000 hectares or 64.47 per cent of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories have not yet been gazetted or are still in the process of gazettement, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. He said all state governments have been urged to expedite the gazettement of public open spaces to ensure designated green areas remain protected and are fully utilised for the benefit of the people, particularly by providing green spaces in densely populated areas. He said 23,297.15 hectares of public open spaces have been identified in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories as of December 2025.

items.title: MARA says all 242 sponsored students in France safe amid unrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) is closely monitoring the situation in France to ensure the safety and welfare of its 242 sponsored students amid the unrest. In areas experiencing public transport disruptions, the universities have taken appropriate measures to conduct classes online,” he said in a statement today. “MARA would continue to monitor the situation, with the safety and welfare of its sponsored students remaining a top priority,” he added.

items.title: Queen calls for long-term measures to protect students from haze
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has urged the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive, collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families. “Relevant parties must also develop long-term strategic plans rather than relying solely on temporary solutions when haze emergencies occur,” Her Majesty said. Her Highness Che’ Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor was also present.

items.title: Govt discusses measures to tackle glut of imported vegetables hurting local farmers
items.summary: He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) on the need for imported vegetables and fruits to obtain good agricultural practices certification equivalent to Malaysia Good Agricultural Practices Certification Scheme (myGAP), as well as measures to protect local farmers from competition with imported produce that is not subject to the same standards. Mohamad said imported vegetables and fruits entering Malaysia were currently not required to have good agricultural practices certification equivalent to myGAP in their countries of origin, but remained subject to import requirements, including import permits, phytosanitary certificates issued by exporting countries and inspections by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS). He said commodities facing oversupply included chillies, cabbage, round cabbage, mustard greens, tomatoes and cucumbers, prompting complaints from local growers, including those in Cameron Highlands and Johor.
